# CANDIDATE: OPENING_RANGE_VOLUME_IMBALANCE_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A high-volume breakout of the opening range signals institutional participation and likely continuation. Entry rule: If the first 5‑minute bar volume > 2 × average volume of the same bar over the prior 10 days AND price breaks above the opening range high (ORH) AND VWAP > OR midpoint AND EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA55 (bullish ribbon) then enter long at the break of ORH with stop at the opening range low (ORL). Exit shape: chart-stop at ORL invalidation, TP1 at 1.5R, runner trail 15% off HWM. Regime hint: VIX < 20, time 09:30‑10:30, intraday bias above VWAP.

## Mechanism

Entry triggers on the first 5‑minute bar (09:30‑09:35 ET) when its volume exceeds twice the 10‑day average for that bar, the price breaks above the ORH, VWAP is above the midpoint of the opening range, and the EMA ribbon is bullish (EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA55). Entry is taken at the break of ORH (i.e., the next tick above ORH). Stop is placed at the ORL. Exit: if price moves against the position and touches ORL (chart stop), the trade is closed. Otherwise, TP1 is set at 1.5 times the risk (entry - ORL) added to entry price, and after TP1 is hit, the remaining position trails a stop at 15% below the highest high since entry (HWM). The trade is also forced to close by 10:30 ET if not exited earlier.

1. **Account-size assumption:** The strategy assumes a Safe‑2 account of $2,000 (minimum 3 contracts) per the risk‑rules.md position‑sizing schedule. A $1K paper account would realize approximately 14% of the headline P&L because only 1 contract could be traded (3‑contract floor not met).
2. **Sample bias:** The hypothesis is based on intraday price‑action patterns observed during the 2025‑01‑02 to 2026‑06‑18 period. No formal sample selection has been performed; the idea is derived from screen‑watching and anecdotal observation. Overfit risk is high until a systematic backtest is conducted.

5. **Failure modes:** Worst day – a false breakout that reverses sharply, triggering the ORL stop and then continuing against the position; max drawdown could exceed 50% of allocated capital if multiple consecutive false breakouts occur; blow‑up scenario – a volatility expansion (VIX > 30) that invalidates the VWAP > OR midpoint and EMA ribbon conditions, causing the strategy to stay flat while the market trends, missing large moves.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (cannot estimate what percentage of P&L would come from the top‑5 days without a backtest).
